claim: The wave-data table is reached through the pointer FDB WVTAB in the block-71 pointer list.
The WVTAB LANDERS block caps simultaneous landers at MAX=20 (row 1, byte 0).
LANDERS start each of waves 1-4 at 15,20,20,20 (the WVTAB W1-W4 column).
The WVTAB TIES (baiters) block caps them at MAX=3.
TIES arrive on the schedule 0,3,4,5 across waves 1-4.
The WVTAB PROBES block caps them at MAX=6.
PROBES arrive on the schedule 0,1,3,4 across waves 1-4.
The WVTAB SCHITZOS block caps them at MAX=10.
SCHITZOS have zero WVTAB spawns in waves 1-4 (0,0,0,0) — they arrive by other means.
The WVTAB SWARMERS block caps them at MAX=10.
SWARMERS have zero WVTAB spawns in waves 1-4 (0,0,0,0) — they arrive by other means.
The WVTAB WAVE TIME block carries MAX=30.
WAVE TIME counts down 30,25,20,16 across waves 1-4.
The WVTAB WAVE SIZE block carries MAX=5.
WAVE SIZE is 5 in each of waves 1-4.
GTWV00 subtracts the GA4 cadence from the wave number repeatedly — "NEW GUYS EVERY NTH WAVE".

source.verbatim: GTWV00	SUBA	XTEMP	NEW GUYS EVERY NTH WAVE

claim: On a wave that is a multiple of the cadence, PTARG is loaded with 10 — ten new guys.
The per-wave lookup clamps the wave to 4 (CMPA #4) so waves beyond 4 reuse the W4 column.
The clamped wave is offset by 3 (ADDA #3) to index the W column within each 8-byte block.
The GA4 "RESTORE WAVE #" adjustment — the "new guys every Nth wave" cadence — defaults to $05.
